scope: Committed native guardian SIGKILL with live work, automatic selected-native reacquisition, and normal managed return
qualification: Each TV migrated normally, then a separate owned systemd timer delivered one SIGKILL to the freshly authenticated committed guardian after checking boot, PID, start ticks, executable and production-unit MainPID. The coordinator remained running and unchanged.

A live job wrote one witness and slept across the fault boundary. Automatic held-bootstrap acquisition restored selected native under the original committed transaction and unchanged selection history. The ordinary worker reported stale guardian reconciliation; the job became interrupted with unknown exit code and its witness remained singular.

Production and activation receipts and a completed native job record remained byte-identical across reacquisition. Normal return to managed preserved the completed native result, the interrupted job and the original managed fixture. Only owned test jobs and scopes were removed; prior retained job hashes and enrollment were preserved.

The independent 300-second .NET SDK rescue was armed for each trial and disarmed after verified recovery and cleanup. Both TVs finished managed-ready and settled on their original boots with SDK on loopback.
limits: This service path admits only a complete schema-4 ready journal bound to the last accepted runtime. Partial startup or job-persistence metadata, foreign or changed evidence, unreaped identities and nonempty units still refuse. Wider interruption boundaries remain open.
No reboot, standby, whole-TV OOM, broad pressure, endurance or native-default observation was performed. This is a bounded same-boot guardian-loss case.

The unchanged managed API refuses same-boot saved interrupted job.forget. Returned records were first verified, then only the owned interrupted fixture was removed using exact-byte and process-disappearance guards. This existing managed limitation remains open.
The .NET capability-entry bridge, managed worker fallback and independent SDK rescue remain deployed. Native-only capability entry is still unqualified.
The historical 0.7.40 QN90A command-fault timeout and earlier paused S90D coordinator exit remain unexplained; this trial neither repeats those conditions nor establishes their causes.
